purpose: Seed NOEMA's cognition/neurophenomenology source family with reviewed discovery metadata. These records are not approved claims or evidence.

records.title: Dissociative trance and spirit possession: Challenges for cultures in transition
records.candidate_use: Cross-cultural framework for distinguishing culturally patterned possession/trance from clinical dissociative disorder.
records.guardrail: Phenomenological overlap does not make culturally sanctioned possession a disorder.

records.title: A critical review of dissociative trance and possession disorders: etiological, diagnostic, therapeutic, and nosological issues
records.candidate_use: Candidate phenomenology and differential-classification source for trance/possession.
records.guardrail: Clinical case literature is not a prevalence estimate for ritual possession populations.

records.title: Dissociative experience and cultural neuroscience: narrative, metaphor and mechanism
records.candidate_use: Key integrative framework joining neuropsychological mechanism with sociocultural construction and presentation.
records.guardrail: Avoid either/or framing in which an experience must be purely biological or purely cultural.

records.title: Religion, spirituality, and epilepsy
records.candidate_use: Modern review of epilepsy/religious experience and historical-retrodiagnosis limits.
records.guardrail: The review explicitly warns that retrospective epilepsy claims for famous religious figures are weak and that the relationship has been overstated.

records.title: Epilepsy and Ecstatic Experiences: The Role of the Insula
records.candidate_use: Mechanism candidate for rare ecstatic auras involving clarity/certainty and anterior-insula/interoceptive processing.
records.guardrail: A mechanism observed in rare focal epilepsy does not explain ordinary mystical or religious experience generally.

records.title: Autism and Religion
records.candidate_use: Candidate literature map for autism, cognition, religion and cultural fit.
records.guardrail: Modern autism/religiosity findings cannot be projected backward onto historical religious specialists.

records.title: The Intersection of Faith and Neurodiversity: Unraveling Religiosity in Autistic Adolescents-A Critical Review Analysis
records.candidate_use: Candidate contemporary neurodiversity/religiosity source with multidimensional framing.
records.guardrail: Adolescent contemporary studies do not validate historical-role analogies.

records.title: The role of mental illness in the European witch hunts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries: an assessment
records.candidate_use: Counterevidence to simple psychopathology explanations of witch hunts.
records.guardrail: Accusation records are social/historical documents and cannot be treated as diagnostic case notes.

records.title: Criticisms of the psychopathological interpretation of witch hunts: a review
records.candidate_use: Methodological critique of psychiatric reductionism in witch-hunt historiography.
records.guardrail: Historical witchcraft accusation is not evidence of mental illness or neurodivergence.

records.title: The rhythms of trance: Cultural phenomenology and neural mechanisms of music-induced non-ordinary states of consciousness
records.candidate_use: High-value bridge between anthropology and neuroscience of music-induced trance.
records.guardrail: Shared induction mechanisms do not establish shared ritual meaning or historical descent.

forbidden_outputs: modern prevalence projected into historical populations
biomedical mechanism treated as complete explanation of cultural meaning
